title: The Holiday Hangover Korea Has a Name For

slides.headline: Today Korea wakes up **with a holiday hangover.**
slides.note: No drinking required. The news, clinics and family group chats all call it the same thing.

slides.headline: It is called **myeongjeol jeunghugun**
slides.body: 명절 증후군, literally "holiday syndrome." Every Chuseok (추석) and Lunar New Year, Korean news runs stories on it.

slides.headline: The body **keeps the receipts**
slides.body: Headaches, indigestion, stiff shoulders and a sore back. Days of sitting on the floor, cooking and overeating add up.

slides.headline: The heaviest load **lands in the kitchen**
slides.body: Traditionally daughters-in-law fry jeon, pan-fried fritters, for hours at the husband's family home. That is the classic picture.

slides.headline: dishes. **No frying required.**
slides.body: In 2022 Sungkyunkwan (성균관), Korea's top Confucian body, said a Chuseok table needs about nine dishes, and no jeon.

slides.headline: Everyone has **their own version**
slides.body: The driver stuck for hours on the highway. The job seeker dodging questions. The parents who cooked for everyone, then cleaned up.

slides.headline: Think Thanksgiving, **three days running**
slides.body: Now picture cooking it on the floor, at your in-laws', with every relative dropping by. That is the scale Koreans mean.

slides.headline: Families are **rewriting the holiday**
slides.body: Splitting the days between both sides, buying jeon instead of frying it, or skipping the trip for a vacation.

slides.headline: One holiday, **one recovery day**
slides.body: Today Korea is full, sore and on the road home. Holiday syndrome is the price, and more families are cutting it.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
The day after Chuseok, a lot of Korea wakes up with a holiday hangover, and Koreans have a name for it: myeongjeol jeunghugun (명절 증후군), holiday syndrome.

Headaches, indigestion, stiff shoulders, a sore back. Three days of cooking on the floor, long drives and a house full of relatives will do that. The classic picture is the daughter-in-law frying jeon for hours, but drivers, job seekers and tired parents all get their own version.

In 2022 even Sungkyunkwan, Korea's top Confucian body, said the ancestral table needs about nine dishes and no frying. Families are listening: splitting the days, buying the jeon, or taking a trip instead.

What does the day after a big family holiday look like where you live?
reply: One thing that did not fit on the cards: the famous rule for the ancestral table, red fruit on the east and white on the west, is not in the old Confucian ritual texts at all. Sungkyunkwan said so in 2022, after generations of families arguing over it. What holiday rule in your family turned out to be something nobody could trace?
fact_check: 성균관의례정립위원회 2022-09-05 발표: 전 안 부쳐도 됨, 기본 6가지(송편·나물·구이·김치·과일·술) + 육류·생선·떡 더해 9가지 정도. 홍동백서·조율이시는 옛 예법 문헌에 없음. https://www.hankookilbo.com/News/Read/A2022090512250001195 , https://www.ohmynews.com/NWS_Web/OhmyFact/at_pg.aspx?CNTN_CD=A0002863241
명절 증후군 증상(두통·소화불량·어깨/허리 통증·피로·우울감)은 대표 사례로 서술. https://www.yna.co.kr/amp/view/AKR20220905086700005
'Korean news runs stories on it every holiday'은 통계 아닌 관찰 서술.
가족들이 분산 방문·전 구매·여행을 택한다는 건 사례 서술, 비율 주장 안 함.
2026 추석 연휴 9-24~9-26. 9-26(토)는 연휴 마지막 날이라 'on the road home' 서술.
